# Goibibo Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/goibibo-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/goibibo-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects hotel and flight search data from goibibo.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Goibibo Prices in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-goibibo-hotel-and-flight-prices)
- **Code:** [`goibibo.py`](goibibo.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Flight search](results/flight_search.json) · [Hotel search](results/hotel_search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Goibibo hotel search results, with pagination
- Hotel name, price, rating, amenities, location, and images
- Goibibo flight search results (one-way and round-trip)
- Flight number, airline, fare, duration, stops, and leg details

## Functions

- `scrape_hotel_search(search_text, locus_id, checkin, checkout, adults=2, children=0, rooms=1, max_pages=5)` → `List[Hotel]`: Scrape goibibo hotel search; capture the listing API from the search page then paginate until max_pages (copy locus_id from a hotel-listing URL).
- `scrape_flight_search(origin, destination, departure_date, adults=1, children=0, infants=0, return_date=None)` → `List[Flight]`: Scrape flight search results and return parsed flight data.

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`Hotel`**: `id`, `gi_id?`, `name`, `property_type?`, `star_rating?`, `sold_out`, `total_room_count?`, `categories`, `area?`, `city?`, `country?`, `latitude?`, `longitude?`, `images`, `price?`, `price_with_tax?`, `price_suffix?`, `currency?`, `rating?`, `rating_text?`, `review_count?`, `rating_count?`, `amenities`, `description?`, `url?`
- **`FlightLeg`**: `flight_number?`, `airline?`, `aircraft?`, `departure_city?`, `departure_time?`, `arrival_city?`, `arrival_time?`
- **`Flight`**: `flight_number?`, `airline_code?`, `airline_name?`, `origin_code?`, `origin_city?`, `destination_code?`, `destination_city?`, `departure_time?`, `arrival_time?`, `departure_timestamp?`, `arrival_timestamp?`, `duration?`, `stops?`, `layover_cities`, `legs`, `fare?`, `currency?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`goibibo.py`](goibibo.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"IN"`: country of the proxy
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `auto_scroll` = `True`: scroll the page to load lazy content

## Notes

Goibibo.com can be difficult to scrape because of scraper blocking, so this scraper uses Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker) feature, browser rendering, and session-based requests to capture and paginate Goibibo's internal listing and flight search-stream APIs.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/goibibo-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_hotel_search_scraping`, `test_flight_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
